build.depends_on_note: derived from 14 probe/lib file(s) actually read (reference_items[].path, the scripts in build.harness_commands / artifacts[], their one-hop imports, and the documented whole-tree contract of tools/lib/browser.mjs, gamedata.mjs and combat-node.mjs where reached)

bifurcation.note: Declared before any screenshot was taken. RI-CHR01/02/03/PRG02/PRG03 are structure and number items; RI-JRN01 judges diegesis, which is a question about WHAT IS ON SCREEN AT ALL, not about rendering quality. The screenshots in this verdict are used only as presence/absence evidence (is a room, a person, a question rendered?) and never to score fidelity or art direction. No visual reference item is cited and no Morrowind or modern screenshot is used as a bar.

Visibility is also 0: 0 of the required 9 rootkeeper lines, 0 of 4 topics, 0 of 1 quest, 0 of 3 arbiter encounters.
reference_items.path_to_ten: 1) Wire the sign's effect block into the sim: WILLPOWER must drive focus_max (see the RI-PRG02 remedy), then apply focus_max_multiplier 1.6 for nu-ixtu and gate the regen path on the sign, so a harness run of `--scenario prg-focus-regen --state birthsign=nu-ixtu --frames 3600` shows focus_max = 1.60 x base and a strictly non-increasing focus series while a raj-xul run of the same scenario shows regen. Write that scenario; it does not exist. 2) Author the three ku-vastei arbiter encounters as quest records with obey/refuse outcomes, refuse setting Reputation -15 and spawning a named persistent hostile that then appears in >= 3 encounter tables. 3) Ship the 9 rootkeeper greeting lines (one per sign), the 4 birthsign-gated topics and the 1 birthsign-gated quest that birthsigns.json's own `visibility` object already specifies.

blind_comparisons.question: In which of these two openings is the player's identity produced by something a character in the world is doing for a reason of their own?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: A's official has motives that are visibly his own and not the player's: he says the sex box exists because 'the box is there. It changes nothing. Nothing in this province will treat you differently for it and I have watched for eleven years'; he guesses the race wrong first ('Altmer. — No, of course not, you are not tall enough and you are not smug enough'); and he offers the class routes with 'there are three ways to do this and I do not care which, and neither does the box'. B's beats are recorded from outside the fiction — 'You choose. He writes it down.' — and the person doing the recording has no stated reason of his own. A is the one in which identity is a by-product of somebody else's paperwork.

biggest_gap.what: The entire Writ House creation sequence renders nothing. Driving all 19 census nodes through window.__HARNESS and screenshotting after each at 1920x1080 produces 20 byte-identical PNGs (sha256 7277a273453ac8631c318f3d9120d7b12b7f562b187adabf59fe3ca7b5daaeb5) showing a body standing in an empty green field: no barge hold, no Writ House interior, no Jeeh-Ei, no Warden-Scribe Tuleeh-Ma, no question, no answer options, and document.body.innerText empty at every node. listEntities() returns 0 entities before and after creation. The scene exists only as a JSON state machine whose getCensusState() self-reports full_screen:false, world_visible:true and full_screen_panels:0 — three fields with no rendered counterpart. RI-CHR01's first bar is 'creation is a scene, not a screen'; what shipped is neither, and RI-JRN01's whole Diegesis block (35 of its 100 points) has nothing to measure.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player starting this game is never asked anything by anybody: the best-written material in the piece — a bored official who guesses your race wrong and tells you the sex box changes nothing because he has watched for eleven years — is delivered to no one, so character creation cannot be experienced at all.

remedy.action: Render the census scene over the live 3D view. (1) In game/data/states/writ-house.json, place the two NPC entities the scene already names — jeeh-ei in the barge hold and warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma behind the desk — as real entities with positions and the npcs/writ-house.json records attached, so listEntities() returns >= 2 throughout creation and the speaker named by getCensusState().speaker has a body in the frame. (2) Add a dialogue surface to game/src/render that draws getCensusState()'s `line`, `input.kind` and `input.options` as a bottom-anchored panel occupying <= 55% of frame area with the world rendering behind it, and drives censusAnswer() from real input (press/release on the closed action set, so keyboard, gamepad and touch all work). (3) Move the camera to the interior named in getCensusState().interior for the duration of the scene. (4) Render readWrit() as an openable inventory object rather than a string returned by an API.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run tools/harness/critic-w1-07a.mjs. Acceptance is met when: (a) the 19 creation-node screenshots yield >= 15 distinct sha256 hashes rather than 1; (b) listEntities() returns >= 1 NPC entity at every node and the entity id equals getCensusState().speaker at the node where that speaker talks; (c) the line returned by getCensusState() appears as rendered text in the frame at every node, with opaque non-world UI <= 55% of frame area and 0 frames whose background is uniform over >= 90% of the frame; (d) the whole sequence is completable on keyboard only and on gamepad only. RI-JRN01 M5/M6 then become measurable and the item can leave 0.

secondary_observations.what: The build does not boot at HEAD. game/data/index.json references dialogue/topics/thorn.json, which does not exist at commit 65275dc (the entry arrived with the W1-18 commit); loadData() throws and window.__HARNESS.ready() fails, so no harness measurement of any kind is possible on the repository as checked out. Every measurement in this verdict was taken in a clean git worktree at the same commit with that single index entry removed. It is not W1-07's defect but it is the state of the tree the piece was delivered into, and it blocks every other critic too.

The builder's checkpoint claims 12/12 on RI-CHR02 method 8; at HEAD it is 10/12. Running the item's literal command for all three races at seed 1337 produces zero Khajiit AGGRO transitions in 1,800 frames, because closest approach is 18.198 m in all three runs and the Khajiit band is 12 m. The builder's own report records a Khajiit AGGRO at 11.956 m at f=514 and a Saxhleel AGGRO at f=90, so player locomotion along this road changed between the W1-07 commit and HEAD. tools/analysis/ar3-encounter-test.mjs is a good tool and it now exits 1.

getEncounterState('dres-raid-party') reports race:'saxhleel' for a Dunmer, a Khajiit and a Nord when setCharacter is called and the state reloaded within the same browser session. The encounter's race binding is latched at first spawn and is not re-derived on state reload, so the AR-3 behaviour is only correct in a fresh process.

Three of the four world states RI-CHR02's and RI-CHR03's methods name by id do not exist: helstrom-market (CHR02 m7), stormhold-street (CHR02 m9) and rootlands-well-graph (CHR03 m3). Only writ-house and wld-dres-raid-road are loadable of the states this piece needs. Every consequence the piece claims is therefore reachable only as a harness oracle function, never through a merchant, a guard or a well.

setCharacter silently accepts and discards an unknown key: passing second_birthsign:'nu-ixtu' returns birthsign_second:null with no error, while birthsign_second:'nu-ixtu' works. A harness verb that drops a field it does not recognise will produce a false negative for the next critic who runs RI-CHR03 method 9.

The written content is the strongest thing in the piece and should not be lost when the delivery is rebuilt. The Warden-Scribe's race read-back, the sex-box speech, the three-routes line and the stamped writ (with its caste line and bounty-ledger reference TW-DUN-SCO) are Morrowind-register work; the blind pick on RI-JRN01's discriminating question landed on ours on the text alone.

arbitration_questions.question: AR-2 check B5 makes any price denominated in souls an automatic fail of the piece (seam S15: 'souls level you and ONLY level you'). RI-CHR03 §5 prices the birthsign re-cut at 'all souls currently carried, to a minimum of 25,000', and RI-CHR01 §7 endorses it. Which governs when the re-cut is actually built?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: S15 is absolute: the moment souls buy anything other than a level, the currency stops being a levelling resource and becomes gold, and every soul-spend decision in RI-PRG01's curve is contaminated. B5 says any such price fails the piece.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: The re-cut is not a purchase, it is a sacrifice: RI-CHR03 §5 prices it in souls precisely so it can never be a routine optimisation, and pricing it in gold would make it a shrine you visit before a boss fight — the exact failure RI-CHR03's How-we-lose names. A one-per-save irreversible sacrifice is not a shop.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-CHR02 method 1 asserts 'no two races have identical skill sets', but RI-CHR02 §1's own table gives Nord and Orsimer the same five skills (Greatweapons, Axes & Maces, Shieldcraft, Survival, Athletics) at different values. Is 'skill set' the set of skill ids or the id-to-value map?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: n/a — this is a corpus self-consistency question, not a seam collision. Recorded here because CRITIC-DOCTRINE §7.4 forbids a critic inventing the ruling.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: The build reproduces the corpus table faithfully, so charging the failure to the build would punish fidelity. Either method 1 should read 'no two identical skill PROFILES', or one cell of the Nord or Orsimer row should change. The builder declared this in game/data/progression/KNOWN-GAPS.json with the same reasoning and this critic reached it independently.

notes: Ordering, per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8: the gap ledger for these subsystem paths was read only after raw measurement was complete. Two mapping decisions are recorded here so they can be audited or overruled. (1) RI-CHR01, RI-CHR02, RI-CHR03, RI-PRG02 and RI-PRG03 all aggregate min-over-axes and all have at least one axis sitting at its own 0 band, so each has a native score of 0. Mapping all five to ladder 0 would assert that the thing does not exist, which the artifacts contradict — the data model is complete, the 112-point invariant holds across 140 pairs, the 12x10 matrix is authored rather than generated (sigma 9.894, all rows and columns distinct, one genuine neutral row) and the disposition oracle produces the item's own 74/48/24/6/0 live. The ladder scores of 1-3 are therefore assigned as the lowest band that is not a claim of non-existence, with the zero axes named in each item's checks and why_not_ten. (2) The overall score uses mean rather than min so the number carries information about how much was built; the gate is enforced by status and by the hard fails, not by the mean. The single sentence that summarises the piece: everything a save file would contain was built correctly, and almost nothing that reads a save file was.
